Records
The County Clerk is elected for a 4 year term and is responsible for keeping the following records:
Births
Deaths
Marriages
Each of the above are available back to 1867. To request records, please click here to view the instructions . Request form available below.
Assumed Names
Military discharge papers
Applications
In addition, the Clerk's Office processes applications for:
Concealed Pistol Permits
Notary Bonds
Other Responsibilities
The County Clerk administers all election functions required by law. The Clerk is responsible for training the local clerks and election inspectors.
The County Clerk serves as the clerk for the Board of Commissioners, Board of Canvassers and the Jury Board.
The County Clerk's Office processes all payroll and human resource functions as well as all accounts payable.

The Register of Deeds is the official recording office for all land records in Keweenaw County.
Records
The office is responsible for recording the following:
Deeds
Mortgages
Satisfactions/Discharges
Assignments
Tax Liens
UCC/Financing Statements
Public Records: All records are available to the public except for Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavits which are not public record. Our computer images begin in October of 2010 and we will be adding historic images soon.
Deeds Search
Deeds Search-Searching of the Keweenaw County Register of Deeds database is available both in-person and online. Seach and copy fees may apply.
Free in-person search on the Keweenaw County database can be done at the Courthouse.
Laredo is subscription based, designed for users who consistently search. This is the same software that is used in the Register of Deeds. For a monthly fee, users will be able to search records from their home or office 24 hours per day, 7 days a week.
Tapestry is designed for the occasional user. All documents are available from October 2010 to present. (Historical images are currently being worked on.) Users pay $8.75 per search and $1 per page for each document PRINTED.

The Register of Deeds is now accepting documents submitted electronically (eRecording). Save time and postage by contacting Simplifile at 1-800-460-5657.
